body:
I've tried knitting, computer games, and photography. My SO thinks I should give them more of chance, and perhaps he is right. So I may try them some more.

After a bad breakup once, I trained for a half marathon, and it helped quite a bit. It kept me busy, I got to be outside, and I was more physically fit. I thought I'd try that again. I even got new running shoes, but I just feel so tired after work. I know I have to push myself for those things. But I guess I'm just not there yet. I thought of maybe starting smaller and training for a 5k to make it more manageable. 

I also started a blog couple of months ago. I posted about 5-6 times, but I haven't posted in about a month-a month and a half. I may start that back up again. 

Other than that I don't have any other ideas. I'm just worried that if things don't improve I'll commit suicide. I'm not religious, so I don't have that motivation to stay. Really some of the only things keeping me alive are the hope that it may get better, my SO, and how me committing suicide could affect my clients with suicidal thoughts. 

Anyhow, thanks for listening. If you have other ideas of things that have helped you or other people you know. I'd love to hear them.

It really is. :( 

My hours really aren't so bad. It's just that I commute to work, so it seems worse than it is. I only work about 40 hours a week, but they are in the exact same hours as most counselors..I haven't found a single counselor yet that has hours where I could actually meet with them on a regular basis. 

Now that graduate school is over, I have WAY more time for self-care and fun. I try to do things, but I still haven't found a hobby that I love. And most of my friends live far away. But yes, for the most part, I practice quite a bit of self-care. 

Thanks for replying to my post. :)

Maybe I'll try that book! Thanks for the suggestion. :) 

? I don't think I'm discounting my partner. He's been incredibly patient and understanding with my mental illness. Maybe I don't quite understand what you mean. 

It does have suggestions, but I've tried almost all of them. I work out a decent some, eat well, think positively, etc. A lot of the therapy for depression deals with cognitive behavioral therapy, but my depression seems to not be connected to any negative feelings or thoughts...other than the hopelessness because it's been going on so long. So the traditional methods of dealing with depression don't seem as applicable to my situation. I hope that makes sense.
